summary.title: How to Deploy Software
summary.one_liner: Deployments should be boring, straightforward, and stress-free, and this long essay by Zach Holman covers the high-level collaboration, safety, and pace aspects of shipping code to production.
takeaways: Deploys should be as boring, straightforward, and stress-free as possible.
Deployment is largely a collaboration problem: teams should regularly evaluate how they work together when shipping.
The essay focuses on high-level process aspects (collaboration, safety, pace) rather than low-level, language-specific details.
Good deploy processes are easy for new employees to understand, defensive against errors, and well-tested before users see changes.
summary.summary: This is an opinionated essay by Zach Holman on software deployment, drawing on his five years at GitHub and a year of advising tech companies on their deploy workflows. It frames the core goal as making deploys boring and low-stress, and organizes the discussion around collaboration, safety, and pace. The author states that he deliberately skips low-level, language-specific details. The intro also credits reviewers from Heroku, GitHub, and Slack and mentions Dockbit, a startup he advises that focuses on collaborative deploys.
